definitions.explanation: a person who challenges a champion or authority, or takes on a difficult endeavor

examples.japanese: {挑戦者|ちょうせんしゃ}が{現|あらわ}れた。
{若|わか}い{挑戦者|ちょうせんしゃ}が{王者|おうじゃ}に{立|た}ち{向|む}かった。
examples.english: A young challenger stood up against the champion.

examples.japanese: {世界|せかい}タイトルマッチで{挑戦者|ちょうせんしゃ}が{見事|みごと}な{逆転|ぎゃくてん}{勝|が}ちを{収|おさ}めた。
examples.english: The challenger achieved a brilliant come-from-behind victory in the world title match.

notes:
Composed of {挑戦|ちょうせん} (challenge) + {者|しゃ} (person). Refers to someone who challenges a current holder of a title, record, or position. Frequently used in sports and competitive contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {挑戦者|ちょうせんしゃ}が{現|あらわ}れる: a challenger appears
- {挑戦者|ちょうせんしゃ}を{迎|むか}える: to face a challenger
- {挑戦者|ちょうせんしゃ}を{退|しりぞ}ける: to fend off a challenger
- {永遠|えいえん}の{挑戦者|ちょうせんしゃ}: eternal challenger

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {対戦相手|たいせんあいて}: opponent — neutral term for the other side in a match
- {競争相手|きょうそうあいて}: competitor — rival in a general competitive context
- {挑戦|ちょうせん}: challenge — the act itself rather than the person
